title: Ailytics Raises US$7.4M Series A to Scale Vision AI Safety Across APAC, the US and the Gulf
summary: The Singapore deep tech startup turns existing industrial CCTV into a real-time safety and operations layer, with local teams now landing in the US, Japan, Australia and the Gulf.
description: Ailytics raises a US$7.4M Series A led by Tin Men Capital to scale vision AI safety across APAC, the US and the Gulf using the CCTV worksites already own.
html:
Most industrial worksites already have cameras. The footage is there. The problem has never been the hardware: nobody was watching until after the incident.

Today we're announcing the milestone that changes what's possible on those sites: Ailytics has raised US$7.4 million in a Series A round led by Tin Men Capital, with Singapore's SEEDS (part of SG Growth Capital) and Safie, Japan's largest cloud camera company, also participating, alongside one of Japan's largest construction companies, family offices, and returning investors.

Why the cameras were never the problem

Most worksite footage sits on a server somewhere, reviewed only after something goes wrong. That's backwards. An incident that's already happened is a cost you can never recover. The goal is to catch the risk in the second it appears.

Ailytics turns the CCTV a customer already owns into a real-time safety and operations layer. No rip-and-replace, no new camera estate. Our platform connects over standard RTSP/ONVIF and runs computer-vision detection on edge, on-premise, or cloud, whatever the site demands.

The result, across more than 400 deployments in 15 countries: customers report a 73 per cent reduction in total recordable incident rate and 84 per cent fewer safety non-compliances. Our platform has detected more than 5.7 million hazards and monitored more than 500 million square metres of active worksites, from the US and Australia to the Netherlands, Hong Kong, Japan, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

Nearly three million workers around the world die each year from work-related accidents and disease, with heavy industries like construction, manufacturing and marine responsible for 63 per cent of all fatal occupational injuries. In Singapore alone, construction, manufacturing and transport accounted for more than half of all fatal workplace accidents in 2025. That's the reality our platform exists to change, and it's why we build for the conditions, not the lab.

Built for the conditions, not the lab

Five years of live deployments have taught us something a controlled environment never could: the real world is wet, dark, dusty and obstructed.

In June, we deployed AilyssaX, our contextual reasoning engine, to process contextual scenes on the move and verify multi-step procedures. It runs on decades-old cameras, through rain, dust and poor lighting, where models built in clean environments often break down.

"Advanced computer vision can run on a decade-old camera and handle safety, productivity and security from one platform," says Prateek Manocha, Co-Founder and CTO. "This round lets us build our own domain-specific models and keep the cost of running AI low as demand grows."

From Singapore deep tech to global enterprise AI

Ailytics began in 2019 as a joint research project between NUS and Singapore's Housing & Development Board. We cut our teeth on HDB and JTC projects with contractors including Woh Hup, Obayashi and Soilbuild, and today run large deployments at NatSteel, the PaxOcean shipyard in Indonesia, DHL, Rome's Leonardo da Vinci International Airport, and more than 1,000 cameras on the Changi Airport Terminal 5 build.

"In five years, we've grown from a Singapore start-up into a platform running more than 400 deployments across 15 countries and four continents," says Lenard Tan, Co-Founder and CEO. "In the US, we intend to win the mid-sized industrial companies that incumbents have priced out. We are building a global industrial AI company from Singapore."

That ambition earned the backing of investors who've been with us from the start. Tin Men Capital, which led our earlier pre-Series A, has worked with us on market selection, commercial strategy and international expansion.

"This is a team that truly understands customer workflow and industry compliance requirements to deliver value to massive legacy industries," says Jeremy Tan, Co-founder and Managing Partner at Tin Men Capital. "Ailytics has reached 15 markets at very robust unit economics and client churn below 1 per cent. We definitely want to be right behind the team as it scales globally."

Our memorandum of understanding with Safie, a supplier to 29 of Japan's 30 largest construction companies, deepens our position in Japan, one of our priority markets.

What's next

This round puts local teams on the ground in the US, Japan, Australia and the Gulf, and extends the platform deeper into manufacturing, logistics, oil and gas, maritime and mining. Our biggest chapter is still ahead.

If you run a worksite where safety, productivity or security currently depends on someone catching it on camera after the fact, we'd love to show you what a real-time layer looks like.

About Ailytics

Ailytics is a Singapore-headquartered deep tech and vision AI software startup. Its proprietary Ailyssa platform applies advanced computer vision and vision language model (VLM) capabilities to existing CCTV to detect risks, improve compliance and optimise operations across heavy industries.
